name: openGauss
tagline: Huawei-originated open-source RDBMS forked from PostgreSQL, with in-memory and column engines.
description: openGauss is an enterprise relational database that Huawei open-sourced in 2020 from the kernel of its GaussDB, itself forked from PostgreSQL 9.2. It has diverged substantially: a thread-pool architecture instead of process-per-connection, the MOT in-memory engine, row (Astore/Ustore) and column storage, AI-assisted tuning and indexing, and in 7.0 a DataVec vector engine. It is widely deployed in China across banking, telecom and government as part of domestic-database programs, with many vendors shipping commercial distributions on top of it. Outside China, adoption, documentation quality in English and ecosystem support are limited.

pricing.notes: Free; commercial distributions and support from Huawei (GaussDB) and Chinese vendors such as Enmotech.

scale.notes: Primary-standby with quorum replication; distributed scale-out is offered through ShardingSphere-based or commercial GaussDB editions.

strengths: Thread-pool model handles many connections without an external pooler
MOT in-memory engine for latency-sensitive OLTP tables
Row and column storage in one engine for mixed workloads
Strong security features: TDE, full-encrypted queries, row-level security
Large Chinese ecosystem of commercial distributions and ARM (Kunpeng) optimization
weaknesses: Forked from PostgreSQL 9.2, so modern Postgres extensions rarely work unmodified
English documentation and community support are limited
Linux-only, best tested on openEuler and Kunpeng hardware
Few managed offerings outside Huawei Cloud
useCases: Chinese banking and telecom core systems
Domestic-database replacements for Oracle in China
HTAP workloads mixing row and column tables
notIdealFor: Teams relying on the PostgreSQL extension ecosystem
Organizations outside China needing vendor support
